process_description: Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01 acts as a buffer between the existing process unit and the Hydrogen Production Unit (HPU). Liquid naphtha is received from the existing process unit and stored in 100T-01, which is designed for approximately five days of HPU inventory. The tank operates at 38 °C and 0.01 barg, with design limits of 43/-8 °C and 0.07/-0.06 barg. Vapor loss and flammable-mixture formation are controlled by an internal floating roof and nitrogen blanketing. Nitrogen in-breathing is controlled by PCV-0101, while out-breathing is routed through PCV-0102 to an activated carbon canister and then to atmosphere. Secondary tank pressure protection is provided by PVV-0102 and EH-0101. Liquid level interlocks prevent overfilling and dry running: LSHH-0102 under IS-09 closes the naphtha inlet shutdown valve, while LSLL-0102 under IS-10 trips pumps 100P-01A/B and closes the outlet shutdown valve. The naphtha transfer pumps 100P-01A/B send naphtha to the HPU at 37 m3/h, equivalent to approximately 24,496 kg/h at 660 kg/m3. A minimum circulation flow of 8.6 m3/h is returned to the tank through RO-0101. Emergency isolation IS-28 is initiated by HS-0101A/B and closes inlet/outlet shutdown valves while tripping the transfer pumps.
intention: The intention of the Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01 system is to provide a stable buffer inventory between the existing process unit and the Hydrogen Production Unit (HPU), allowing continuous naphtha feed to the HPU during upstream process interruption or outage. The tank is intended to receive liquid naphtha from the existing process unit, store approximately five days of inventory, and supply naphtha to the HPU through the Naphtha Transfer Pumps 100P-01A/B at a nominal flow rate of 37 m3/h, equivalent to approximately 24,496 kg/h at a density of 660 kg/m3. The intended operating envelope is 38 °C and 0.01 barg, with design limits of 43/-8 °C and 0.07/-0.06 barg. The system is also intended to maintain safe naphtha storage by minimizing vapor loss and flammable-mixture formation through the internal floating roof, nitrogen blanketing, pressure-controlled in-breathing via PCV-0101, and controlled out-breathing via PCV-0102 to the activated carbon canister. Protection objectives include overfill prevention by LSHH-0102 and IS-09, pump dry-running prevention by LSLL-0102 and IS-10, continuous pump minimum-flow protection through RO-0101, thermal relief of trapped liquid by PSV-0101, secondary tank pressure/vacuum protection by PVV-0102 and EH-0101, and total emergency isolation through IS-28 initiated by HS-0101A/B.

connections.node: Naphtha Tank Storage (100T-01) with Naphtha Transfer Pump (100P-01A/B)
connections.node_boundary: Includes the inlet transfer line from the existing Process Unit / B-L to Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01, the tank storage section, the outlet/suction transfer lines from 100T-01 to Naphtha Transfer Pumps 100P-01A/B, the pump discharge transfer line to the Hydrogen Production Unit (HPU), the minimum-flow recycle line from pump discharge back to 100T-01, nitrogen blanketing, controlled vapor out-breathing through activated carbon, pressure/vacuum relief, emergency venting, and drainage to OWS/CSS.
connections.flow_direction: Mainstream liquid naphtha flows from the existing Process Unit / B-L to Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01, then from 100T-01 to Naphtha Transfer Pumps 100P-01A/B, and finally from the pump discharge header to the Hydrogen Production Unit HPU. A minimum-flow recycle stream returns from the pump discharge header to 100T-01 through RO-0101. Nitrogen flows into the tank vapor space through PCV-0101. Tank out-breathing vapor flows from 100T-01 through PCV-0102 and AC-0101 to atmosphere. Relief flow is from 100T-01 to a safe location or atmosphere through PVV-0102 and EH-0101. Drainage flows from the tank area to OWS and CSS.
connections.context: Grouped HAZOP reasoning node for the complete naphtha buffer storage and transfer function. This node supports mainstream cause-consequence reasoning across the inlet transfer line, tank inventory, blanketing/venting, outlet isolation, pump suction, pump discharge, recycle, relief, and drainage systems. Causes at one location may propagate to other parts of the node; for example, failure or unintended closure of UV-0101-IN can reduce tank inventory, eventually create low-low level conditions, trip or starve 100P-01A/B, and interrupt feed to the HPU. Similarly, outlet valve failure, low tank level, minimum-flow recycle failure, vent blockage, nitrogen failure, or relief failure can create broader consequences such as tank overfill, tank vacuum, tank overpressure, vapor emission, flammable atmosphere formation, pump dry running, pump deadheading, inadequate HPU feed, trapped-liquid overpressure, or failure of emergency isolation.
